text:
sarah: Quick question — POC with Acme asking for our incident / breach notification commitments. They want: timelines, who we CC, and what we can promise in the POC contract. @mike can you confirm what we typically say for hosted vs private deployments?

mike: Short version: Hosted API — initial acknowledgement within 72h of detection, periodic updates, and a completed IR summary usually within 7-30 days depending on complexity. For POCs we aim for ~7-14 days for the first full report.

mike: Private/VPC/on-prem — customer controls infra; we notify customer within 72h of confirming an issue in our software or service. We do not take over customer infra for forensics unless explicitly contracted.

julia: For Dedicated (reserved) pools we have enhanced telemetry and can usually produce an initial triage within 24-48h. Worth calling this out to buyers — Dedicated = faster triage.

lee: Legal note: do not promise regulator reporting timelines (e.g., GDPR 72h) as our obligation unless contractually agreed. We can promise to "notify" within 72h and provide updates, but avoid guaranteeing root cause or filed reports in that window.

sarah: Got it. What's the minimal notify template we should send for a POC buyer?

mike: Quick template (use for initial email):

```
Subject: Redwood Inference — Security Incident Notification
Date: {date}
Customer: {customer}
Summary: One-line description of the issue and impacted components
Initial action: What we’ve done so far (isolate, rotate keys, disable endpoint)
Estimated scope: e.g., no customer data exposed / limited tokens / unknown
Next update ETA: {time}
Contacts: ir@redwood.ai, customer success rep {name}
```

nina: Add a line for customer-side contacts + any legal/regulatory contacts they require. Also include a short mitigation checklist for them to follow immediately.

mike: Operational addendum: for customers that request SIG/CAIQ evidence during an incident, we can attach the incident artifact checklist (logs, timeline, mitigations). For formal forensic work we charge at T&M unless the SOW includes it.

sarah: Finance question — do we ever cover forensics costs for POCs?

lee: Standard POC policy = forensics at customer expense. If sales wants to include forensic work, that requires approval from revenue ops/legal and explicit language in the SOW.

julia: Also note: for Dedicated customers we sometimes offer a one-time forensic snapshot as an onboarding credit — useful negotiation lever.

sarah: Who should be CC'd on the initial notify for enterprise buyers?

mike: cc: @lee (legal), @nina (CS), and add internal IR triage (`ir-bot`) to create an incident ticket. Also include the on-call security engineer if severity high.

ir-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4725 — https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-4725 — assigned to mike (security).

sarah: Perfect — I’ll send the template and spin up the ticket if needed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
